newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia July-May budget deficit A$9.645 bln.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia July-May budget deficit A$9.645 bln.

text.p: Australia's underlying budget deficit for the 11 months to May, the first 11 months of fiscal 1996/97, was A$9.645 billion, compared with a A$13.987 billion deficit for the same period a year earlier, Finance Minister John Fahey said on Friday.
The headline balance for the 11 months was a A$5.498 billion deficit, compared with a A$9.525 deficit a year earlier, Fahey said in a statement.
The headline figure excludes windfall items such as asset sales and state government debt repayments.
Government finances are highly seasonal and cannot be extrapolated to a final outcome for the fiscal year to June 30.
Fahey said revenue grew 7.8 percent, compared with budget projections of 7.0 percent, and underlying outlays increased 3.3 percent, against a budget estimate of 2.9 percent.
The main spending increases were in welfare payments and the government's tax break for middle and low income families.
The main revenue increases were from higher income tax due to increased wages and jobs growth and increased company tax receipts due to changed collection timing.
The government has forecast an underlying deficit of A$6.856 billion in 1996/97 and a headline surplus of A$764 million.
The monthly underlying balance was a A$712 million deficit, compared with a A$1.736 billion deficit a year earlier, and the headline deficit A$841 million, compared with A$1.809 billion.
